counterfactual_missing_items: No clear evidence of distant metastatic disease at initial diagnosis
No mention of other primary malignancies
No alternative explanations for the satellite lesions
decisive_items: Incidentally resected lymph node showed focal involvement
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
response.rationale: R6 is the champion because it has the most comprehensive support from the raw vignette spans, including histopathology findings and lymph node involvement, which are characteristic of melanoma. R5 is the runner-up because it also has strong support from the vignette, but it is more focused on the recurrence aspect, whereas R6 encompasses the overall diagnosis of melanoma.

rejected.why: Too narrow, only focuses on tumor regression due to immunotherapy, without considering the broader diagnosis of melanoma
Only accounts for the immune-mediated reaction, without addressing the underlying diagnosis of melanoma
Too specific to T-VEC-treated melanoma, without considering other aspects of the diagnosis
Although it mentions recurrence, it is an append-only completion and does not provide a complete diagnosis like R6
